conceptual-guide.purpose: Machine-readable metadata for search and indexing
1-3 sentences: what the user will learn from this doc and who it is for
Navigation table (Use Case / Section / Key Call) for multi-section docs where orientation and navigation matter
Orients developers before they read requirements
Explanatory content, placed after working setup
Root cause and resolution for each failure
Links to what comes after, each with a description

feature-doc.purpose: Machine-readable metadata for search and indexing
1-3 sentences: what this feature does and who it is for
Orients developers before they read requirements
Explanatory content, placed after working setup
Root cause and resolution for each known failure
Links to what comes after, each with a description

how-to-guide.purpose: Machine-readable metadata for search and indexing
Human-readable entry point, should be imperative ("Fetch entries using the Delivery API")
1-3 sentences: what the developer achieves by following this guide
Only if the task has meaningfully different paths (for example, REST vs GraphQL)
Only if a concept is required to complete the task and cannot be linked externally
Root cause and resolution for failure modes specific to this task
Links to what comes after, each with a description

setup-guide.purpose: Machine-readable metadata for search and indexing
1-3 sentences: what the developer will have configured after following this guide
Required when the setup differs by environment, runtime, or hosting platform
Blocking and non-blocking requirements, separated, all items link to the resource that fulfills them
Only when understanding a concept is necessary to configure correctly
Root cause and resolution for each known failure mode during setup
Links to what the developer builds or configures next

kickstarter.purpose: Machine-readable metadata for search and indexing
1-3 sentences: what the starter does and what stack it uses
Only if the repo offers meaningfully different configurations (for example, SSR vs SSG variants)
Blocking requirements with links: Node version, package manager, Contentstack stack setup
Clone, install, configure, run steps, each step ends with a verifiable outcome
Conceptual explanation belongs in linked docs, not in the kickstarter
Root cause and resolution for common local-run failures
Links to the conceptual guide, feature docs, or how-to guides the developer should read next

migration-guide.section: SEO front matter (title, description, URL, version)
migration-guide.purpose: Metadata, version field identifies which upgrade this guide covers
States the source and target version explicitly
States when the guide applies, what the breaking change is, and what the reader gains
Orients developers (full migration vs. gradual) before they read requirements
Mandatory: target SDK and runtime versions with links. Optional: background knowledge

migration-guide.required: Required if the API surface changes
migration-guide.purpose: Before/after table covering every renamed type, method, and attribute
One subsection per changed area, each subsection contains a Before block and an After block

migration-guide.required: Required if a partial migration path exists
migration-guide.purpose: Adapter or compatibility pattern for incremental porting
Root cause and resolution for each known failure introduced by the migration
Ordered checklist of every change the developer must make before removing the old dependency
Links to SDK changelog, official migration references, and related docs

getting-started.purpose: Machine-readable metadata for search and indexing
2–3 sentences: what the product does and what the developer will have after following the Quick Start
Routes each developer persona to the correct first doc immediately; placed before Quick Start so developers who know their path can leave fast
Only the blocking items for the Quick Start path; each links to the resource that fulfills it
The single fastest path to a working outcome; time-bounded, one path only, ends with a verifiable outcome
Navigation table organized by developer goal; the developer's map of what exists and where to go next
3–5 links to the most logical reads after Quick Start, each with a one-sentence description
